diagnostics.notes: Both claims are within-group changes in LDL-cholesterol with metformin treatment, so the contrast is comparable. Side A reports metformin significantly reduced LDL-cholesterol at 24 weeks; side B explicitly reports no significant changes in LDL-cholesterol with metformin treatment. This is an explicit no-effect conclusion against a reported effect, so not_replicated applies rather than apparent_contradiction. Populations differ (Japanese T2DM on sitagliptin vs overweight/obese PCOS women), but that difference is contextual and not required for the branch chosen.

source_evidence.quote: Metformin significantly reduced HbA1c and LDL-cholesterol levels and increased HOMA-beta.

orlistat treatment significantly lowered the levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol, fasting blood glucose, and homeostasis model assessment-insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) (P<0.05), while there were no significant changes in above parameters with metformin treatment.

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both findings concern within-group change in LDL-cholesterol with metformin. Side A (PRIME-V RCT) reports metformin significantly reduced LDL-cholesterol levels over 24 weeks, while side B (PCOS RCT) explicitly states there were no significant changes in LDL-cholesterol with metformin treatment. An explicit no-change conclusion against a reported significant effect yields not_replicated.
